agent: Claude Code (Opus 5.5) driving Blender 5.2 through the Blender MCP server

stages.title: Head built purely from code
stages.method: Traced the face silhouette in both photos and lofted an egg-shaped mesh through the outlines, then projected the photos on as texture.
stages.result: Recognisable from 3/4 view only; flat face, smeared blend between photos, painted-on hair.
stages.lesson: Two silhouettes describe an outline, not a face. Geometry needs real 3D information.

stages.title: KeenTools FaceBuilder from 3 photos
stages.method: Installed the add-on from a local folder, drove FaceBuilder's face detection and auto-pinning from Python, baked a 4K texture.
stages.result: Real 3D face form, but only 26/8/4 auto pins; generic average-head shape.
stages.lesson: A morphable model is only as good as the number of well-pinned views.

stages.title: Particle-system hair
stages.method: Painted a scalp vertex group from texture darkness and grew curly children. Six iterations.
stages.result: Looked like a knitted cap; a hidden setting reset hair length to 4 m.
stages.lesson: Un-groomed procedural hair never reads as a specific person's hair.

stages.title: FaceBuilder from 8 video frames
stages.method: Wrote a Swift tool to pull frames, picked 8 angles, auto-pinned all 8, colour-corrected skin and faded the neck.
stages.result: Best face so far; still soft, hair flat.
stages.lesson: More angles beat more resolution for fitting; compression hurts texture.

stages.title: Apple Object Capture from the video
stages.method: Ran on-device photogrammetry, aligned the scan to the FaceBuilder face with ICP (1.4 mm median error) and grafted on the hair shell.
stages.result: Correct overall hair volume, but hair surface came out smooth like a beret.
stages.lesson: Photogrammetry cannot resolve individual curls from compressed video, but it measures volume well.

stages.title: Strand hair grown into the measured volume
stages.inputs: Visual hull of the hair from 8 calibrated views
stages.method: Carved a visual hull from the FaceBuilder cameras, grew ~190k strands combed along the skull with curl and clumping.
stages.result: Read as tight rope curls; temples left bald by an over-aggressive mask.
stages.lesson: Hair likeness is about grooming direction and clump shape, which needs a human (or far better data).

stages.title: Full-resolution photo set
stages.method: Re-ran capture and FaceBuilder on sharp stills.
stages.result: Capture failed: subject turned instead of the camera orbiting, producing a flat mask. FaceBuilder skin sharper but eyes wrong colour.
stages.lesson: Photogrammetry needs a static subject and a moving camera. Selfies break it.

stages.title: Gaussian splat trained on-device
stages.method: Exported camera poses from Object Capture as nerfstudio JSON, trained 15,000 steps in Brush on the M4 GPU, cropped to the head, viewed in a web viewer.
stages.result: First result that truly looks like me; soft, with wall floaters. Not riggable.
stages.lesson: Splats capture likeness and hair best, but can't be animated, so they can't drive eye tracking or costumes.

stages.title: Final model: real eyes, hair, web export
stages.inputs: FaceBuilder head from stage 4, hair volume from stage 6
stages.method: Cut almond eye openings matched to the photo texture, added separate eyeballs with a procedural iris and Damped Track gaze, regrew hair from the real hairline in the texture, baked every material to images, converted 121k hair strands into 6.3k hair cards, exported a 6.9 MB GLB and wired the eyes to the cursor.
stages.result: Clearly me from front, 3/4 and profile; eyes move; runs in a browser. Stylised-realistic, not film quality.
stages.lesson: The right format matters more than the best-looking render: a rigged mesh with separate eyes can do things a splat can't.

stages.title: Fixes from my review: eyes, temples, neck
stages.inputs: My notes after viewing the model in Blender
stages.method: Re-centred each eyeball on its measured eyelid opening; added missing hair roots at the temple corners (there were none between 38 and 62 mm above the eyes) and short sideburns; repainted the neck with sampled skin tone, blended the seam in the shader, and modelled a crew-neck t-shirt fitted to the neck's measured cross-section.
stages.result: Pupils sit centred, no receding corners, clean neck-to-shirt transition.
stages.lesson: A human review pass catches what metrics miss: the agent's measurements were right, but 'looks bald' and 'eyes look sideways' came from looking.
